description: Two oscillators, each with a triangle, a saw and a square, and a set of outputs that compare or mix the two

params.text: Sets the pitch of the first oscillator, -8 to 4 as a power of two around middle C, which is about 1Hz to 4186Hz
Shifts the pitch of the first oscillator by up to a hundred cents either way
Sets the pitch of the second oscillator, -8 to 4 as a power of two around middle C
Shifts the pitch of the second oscillator by up to a hundred cents either way
Scales the first oscillator's first FM jack, 0 to 300 per cent
While on, the first oscillator's FM jacks are added to its frequency in hertz rather than to its pitch in octaves
Scales the second oscillator's first FM jack, 0 to 300 per cent
While on, the second oscillator's FM jacks are added to its frequency in hertz rather than to its pitch in octaves
Sets how close the two waves have to be before the EQ output takes a new sample, 0 to 1 of their height
Sets how far the first oscillator is shifted against the second, 0 to 1 of a cycle
Attenuates the voltage at the Phs jack before it is added to the Phs knob, 0 to 1
Puts the phase of both oscillators back to the start of the cycle
Scales the first oscillator's second FM jack, 0 to 300 per cent
Scales the second oscillator's second FM jack, 0 to 300 per cent
Sets the balance of the mix between the two waves, 0 to 1

inputs.text: Sets the pitch of the first oscillator by cable, 1V per octave added to its knob, one channel per voice
Sets the pitch of the second oscillator by cable, 1V per octave added to its knob
Modulates the first oscillator through the FM knob beside it
Modulates the second oscillator through the FM knob beside it
A trigger here puts the phase of both oscillators back to the start of the cycle
A second modulation of the first oscillator, through the knob beside it
A second modulation of the second oscillator, through the knob beside it
Modulates the balance, -5V to 5V scaled by the Mix knob
Modulates that shift, a tenth per volt scaled by the Phs CV knob

outputs.text: Holds the value of the first wave from the moment the two waves last met, which gives a stepped voltage that follows the beating of the pair
Whichever of the two chosen waves is the higher at that moment
The first chosen wave held inside the size of the second, which folds it back where it goes past
The saw of the first oscillator
The triangle of the first oscillator
The square of the first oscillator
The saw of the second oscillator
The triangle of the second oscillator
The square of the second oscillator
Carries 5V while the first wave is above the second and -5V while it is below
A crossfade between the two chosen waves at the Mix setting

notes: the EQ, LT, Max, Clip and Mix outputs use one wave from each oscillator, chosen in the menu; the six wave outputs are always all three shapes of both
menu: Oversample — works the waves out sixteen times over per sample and filters them, which cuts the aliasing of the square and saw shapes
Block DC — takes the constant offset out of the triangle, saw and mix outputs
Wave A — picks which wave of the first oscillator the comparing outputs use: Tri, Saw or Sqr
Wave B — picks which wave of the second oscillator the comparing outputs use: Tri, Saw or Sqr
